challenges.title: Keeping champions engaged after the launch
challenges.summary: Champions drift away after about six months. They have little time for it in the day job, aren't always sure what to do, and can feel invisible.

quotes.text: Champions need a job, not a badge

helped.text: A monthly fix-it Friday, with snacks.
Giving champions a real task each month.
Asking champions to present their fix at the all-hands meeting, which made other people want to join.

lessons.text: Ask champions what they want before planning.

actions.title: Run a monthly fix-it session
actions.what: Hold a 30-minute fix-it session every month.
actions.needs: A room, a list of small bugs and a host.
actions.sticks: Same day every month, and rotate the host.

actions.title: Shout out a champion of the month
actions.needs: An executive to send the email.

questions.text: Resource mentioned: “W3C planning & managing”. The address on the sheet is cut off at w3.org/WAI/planning-and-, so it needs finding before it can be linked.

challenges.title: Getting budget before something goes wrong
challenges.summary: Money tends to arrive only after complaints, and the budget often sits with IT rather than product. Waiting for legal to push it, or asking for a big programme all at once, hasn't worked.

quotes.text: Small and recurring beats big and one-off
Money follows risk, so show the risk

helped.text: Showing the cost of fixing late compared with fixing early.
Piggybacking on the design system budget.
Bidding for accessibility as part of a design system refresh, so it was never a separate ask.

hindered.text: Asking for a big programme all at once.
Waiting for legal to push it.

lessons.text: Small asks that repeat beat one big ask.
One telecoms company's regulator now asks about accessibility in every review, so the risk argument is getting stronger.

actions.title: Cost two real late fixes
actions.what: Find two real issues that were fixed late, and work out what they cost.

actions.title: Ask for a small recurring budget line
actions.what: Ask for a small recurring line in an existing budget.

actions.title: Share a complaint that cost money
actions.what: Find one complaint that cost money and share it.
actions.sticks: Share a new one every quarter.

questions.text: Who owns the budget: IT or product?

commitments.text: Cost one late fix this month
